name: Metallic Gold
lede: Metallic Gold is a warm yellow, a flat screen stand-in for the look of the metal itself.

sections.title: A swatch for a metal
sections.body:
Metallic Gold in our library comes from a single source, a web list of color names, and is nearly identical to a second listing, *Gold (Metallic)*, 0.3 CIEDE2000 units away [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 would call its position a "strong yellow" (block 84), only 1.0 away, which shows how ordinary the swatch is as a yellow [1]. The same block carries older names, Chrome Yellow (first recorded in 1818) and Paris Yellow (about 1850) [1]. A real gold surface changes color with the light it reflects, which no single swatch can show [2].

For related shades see [[gold]] and [[old-gold]]; the nearest named neighbor of the learning set is [[mustard]], at 3.5 units [1].

sections.title: Gold that makes red
sections.body: Gold has a stranger color history than its swatch suggests. Medieval recipes describe making a red or purple from gold, a subject the *Pigment Compendium* treats under Purple of Cassius [3]. Tiny metallic gold droplets in glass give the ruby color, and the shade depends on the droplets' size, which in turn depends on how the glass is heated [4]. The glassmaker Kunckel made gold-ruby glass in 1689 following earlier recipes of Agricola (1556) and Neri (1612) [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our 23,781-painting archive, a color near this one appears in 213 paintings, 0.9% of the total, as photographed [5]. In 82% of the 225 paintings where it is found it plays an accent, a small bright note and not a field [5]. It is most devoted to Luis Egidio Meléndez, in 9 of his 39 works here, and over-represented in paintings from India, 4.3 times the expected rate [5]. It often shares a canvas with [[mustard-brown]] [5]. Gold leaf and plain yellow paint cannot be told apart in a photograph, so the match is a screen color only [5].
